links.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified AAOS Spanish-language orthopaedic patient education materials
links.outcome: Readability (Fernández-Huerta and SOL grade levels) of AI-adapted vs original materials, plus surgeon-rated accuracy and usefulness
links.effect: Materials at a seventh- to eighth-grade level rose from 32% (25 of 77) originally to 53% (41 of 77) after a single AI simplification attempt (p < 0.001). Only 23% (18) and 16% (12) of adaptations reached the recommended sixth-grade level or below by Fernández-Huerta and SOL respectively. None of the originals met the sixth-grade target. 52% (40) of adaptations were rated accurate and 56% (43) useful.
links.tradeoff: Many adaptations were judged inaccurate (about 48%) or not useful (about 44%) by the orthopaedic surgeon reviewers. Adaptations rated accurate or useful had higher median word counts, so shorter outputs were more likely to be inaccurate or not useful.
links.quote: In comparison, after a single attempt at simplification, AI-adapted materials achieved this reading level in 53% of cases (41 of 77; p < 0.001).

design_hint: reading-level constraint prompt with clinician accuracy review
